title: Adaptive Slice Quarantine Playbook — fieldbook
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working fieldbook for an "adaptive slice quarantine" pattern: a lightweight, automated path to isolate problematic traffic slices during staged activations (micro‑releases, canaries, or A/Bs) while preserving overall availability and measurement continuity. Intended audience: rollout stewards, console product owners, SRE oncall, experiment designers, and solutions engineers.

Why this exists (short):
- Many incidents start as narrow slice failures that propagate due to shared downstreams, cache pollution, or correlated latency.
- We need a fast, low-friction mechanism to pinch off only the affected cohort and route them to a safe fallback variant without killing global traffic.
- Quarantine should be reversible, observable, and auditable.

Core concept and guarantees:
- A "slice" is any orthogonal partition of traffic (user cohort, region, client app version, feature flag bucket).
- Quarantine is an automated (or semi-automated) state that: 1) stops routing new requests in the slice to the experimental variant, 2) routes them to the control/fallback model or cheaper fallback path, 3) tracks counts and preserves sampling for telemetry, 4) emits a standard incident signal to oncall and stakeholders.
- Guarantees: minimal blast radius, preserved analytics continuity (we still record slice membership), deterministic rollback path.

Quarantine decision layers (in order):
1) Fast SLO triggers (automated) — 10m sliding window; 2) Policy guard (cooldown + noisy neighbor check) — automated; 3) Steward confirmation (human gate) — optional for sensitive slices.

Signals we use (primary):
- p50/p95/p99 latency for model respond and end-to-end RPCs
- error rate (model 5xx, request validation failures, malformed outputs)
- quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE-like or embedding similarity drift for rerankers) tied to golden prompt set
- cost spike (tokens per response, downstream DB call rate)
- downstream saturation metrics (queue length, GPU util)

Example automated rule (pseudo):
- IF slice_error_rate > 2% for 10m OR p95_latency(delta_baseline) > 2x for 10m THEN mark-slice:quarantine-auto
- Cooldown: once auto-quarantined, no further automatic re-enable for 30 minutes.

Quarantine choreography (steps for automated path):
1) Detection: alert fires in observability system; quarantine workflow is invoked by the rollout router service.
2) Snapshot: router takes a quick checkpoint of active sessions (ids) and current rollout offset for the slice.
3) Redirect: new requests from slice are routed to fallback model/variant. Existing generated responses are allowed to finish (no in-flight preemption).
4) Telemetry tagging: all subsequent events for that slice are tagged with quarantine=true and quarantine_reason=<signal>.
5) Notification: Slack + email to steward list with one‑click rollback and one‑click acknowledge actions.
6) Data capture: golden prompt set sampling continues against fallback to measure quality regression impact.
7) Recovery: automatic attempt to re-enable after a cooldown if signals return to normal AND a quick synthetic smoke test passes.

Quick rollback and recovery recipes (for oncall):
- Fast unquarantine (if false positive): use console -> slice controls -> re-enable slice (note: this will resume routing but will not re-run canary sampling; consider re-run of synthetic smoke tests).
- Manual quarantine (if automated path fails): toggle flag in rollout service, and execute traffic rewrite rule: 'route where slice_id==X to model:control-v2025-03'. Document timestamp and reason in the incident ticket.

Observability checklist (what to surface immediately):
- Dashboard view: slice trend with baseline overlay (last 7d); map to service maps to see downstreams.
- Top correlated traces (SRE): sample 20 traces from quarantined slice -> annotate root cause hypotheses.
- Golden prompt regressions: % mismatches vs control.
- Cost delta panel: tokens/sec, DB qps.
- Quarantine KPI: time-to-quarantine, time-to-unquarantine, percent of sessions re-routed.

Example KQL/SQL snippets to embed in dashboard (copy-paste friendly):
- Slice error rate (10m):
  SELECT slice_id, count_if(status >= 500)/count(*) as error_rate
  FROM requests
  WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '10' minute
  GROUP BY slice_id
  HAVING slice_id = 'SOME_SLICE'

- P95 latency delta vs baseline (30m):
  WITH cur as (SELECT quantile(0.95) as p95 FROM requests WHERE slice_id='SOME_SLICE' AND timestamp > now() - interval '30' minute),
       base as (SELECT quantile(0.95) as p95_base FROM requests WHERE slice_id='SOME_SLICE' AND timestamp between now() - interval '7' day and now() - interval '6' day)
  SELECT (cur.p95 / base.p95_base) as p95_mult

Operational knobs and policy parameters (suggested defaults):
- Auto quarantine threshold: error_rate > 2% OR p95_mult > 2x over 10m
- Min sample size before action: 50 requests in window
- Auto retry window: 30 minutes after quarantine start
- Max quarantine per slice per 24h: 3 events
- Escalation path: if quarantine persists > 45 minutes -> auto-page SRE leader + PM + engineering owner

Communication templates (Slack/email):
- Auto notification: "[Auto-quarantine] slice=US-web-1 flagged at 2026-02-20T14:12Z. Trigger: p95 latency x2. Routing: shifted to control-v3. Actions: steward acknowledge (link), reopen (link), details (link)."
- Postmortem header: "What happened: timeline, immediate mitigation (slice quarantine), measured impact, root cause hypothesis, follow-up actions."

Safety considerations and edge cases:
- Shared caches and KV pollution: if quarantining one slice increases latency for others due to cache cold starts, consider a temporary warmup route that serves cached prefixes from a pre-warmed pool.
- Statefulness: for sticky sessions, decide whether to follow-session or pin to control for duration of session. Default is follow-session for 5 minutes then pin to control to avoid partial UX oscillation.
- Time-of-day noise: do not act on single-window noise for low-traffic slices; require min traffic threshold.

Testing and runbook drills:
- Quarterly drills: run simulated quarantine using synthetic traffic in staging -> confirm dashboard signals, Slack hooks, and rollback buttons.
- Fire drills: simulate a false-positive quarantine to validate steward flow and re-enable path.

Instrumentation requirements (implementation notes):
- Router must expose a single API to mark slice state (normal, quarantine-auto, quarantine-manual, quarantined, reenabled).
- Telemetry pipeline must support a quarantine boolean flag and quarantine_reason string on events.
- Console UI: single-line inline action for quarantine + reason dropdown + timestamped audit trail.

Open questions / things to decide (short list):
- Do we allow auto-quarantine for enterprise customers with legal SLAs? (proposal: auto-disabled for enterprise by default; steward opt-in).
- How granular should min-sample thresholds be per product? (Izzy to propose per-product defaults)
- Should quarantine always route to the exact control variant or allow a cheaper degraded path? (tradeoffs: observability vs cost)

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Implement router API spec (owner: eng-routing; due: 2026-03-10)
- Wire telemetry tags and sample dashboards (owner: observability; due: 2026-03-12)
- Build console quick-actions UX (owner: product-console; due: 2026-03-24)
- Run staging drill and iterate on thresholds (owner: SRE + data; due: 2026-03-30)

Notes to self (working):
- Keep quarantine UX low-friction: steward should be able to read one timeline and act in <60s.
- Preserve audit trail for compliance: store quarantine_reason + actor + UTC timestamp.
- Keep this doc short and practical; move extended examples into Confluence and link above.

Appendix: short incident scenario (narrative):
- 14:05 synthetic smoke fails p95 -> auto-quarantine of slice "mobile-1". 14:07 slack: auto message with quick-reenable link. 14:12 steward inspects traces, finds upstream DB spike from background task introduced in new model. 14:18 isolate background task and unquarantine after smoke test at 14:25. Total quarantine time: 20m. Customer-visible errors: none (traffic routed to control).

If you have edits, please append with initials and date at the bottom of this doc. 

-- Marco C. (draft notes) 2026-02-20
